Cutadapt 5.2, with dnaio 1.2.4 and xopen 2.1.0: cutadapt
Licences: MIT (LICENSE, LICENSE.dnaio, LICENSE.xopen in this folder). Their compiled parts were generated by Cython
(cython-notices/). The Python they run in is Pyodide 314.0.7 – CPython 3.14.2 compiled with Emscripten 5.0.3 – in
../../pyodide/314.0.7/, unchanged (one copy, which Bracken's Python programs use too): its notices, and those of the
libraries in it (CPython, Emscripten, libffi, hiwire, xz, zstd, SQLite, bzip2, zlib), are in runtime-notices/ (see
runtime-notices/README.md). THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt lists them.
Pyodide and hiwire are under the Mozilla Public License 2.0: their source code is in
../../../licenses/sources/ (pyodide-314.0.7.tar.gz,
hiwire-6a1e67280a15d929ebeceee54a6358c9c8d5f697.tar.gz).
Upstream sources: Cutadapt https://github.com/marcelm/cutadapt (cutadapt-5.2.tar.gz on PyPI), dnaio and xopen
(PyPI); Pyodide https://github.com/pyodide/pyodide (release 314.0.7).

Built by the genomics-wasm project (https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, commit bfacba3): Cutadapt's
and dnaio's Cython extensions compiled to WebAssembly with pyodide-build (Emscripten 5.0.3) for CPython 3.14.2, into the
wheels in wheels/; manifest.json names them with their SHA-256, and the page checks them before it installs them.
The page runs each command in a worker of its own (assets/js/python-worker.mjs, adapted from genomics-wasm's
runtime/cutadapt-execute.mjs): it starts that Python, installs the three wheels and runs Cutadapt's command line.
Everything needed to build it again is described in ../../../licenses/genomics-wasm-build/.

The one change to the source (tools/cutadapt/browser.patch there): --cores other than 1 (also 0, "as many as there
are") stops with status 2 – a web page cannot start the processes Cutadapt would use. Trimming is unchanged.
In the workbench's terminal, cutadapt -j N is run on one core, with a note.

Checked against Cutadapt 5.2 with the same dnaio and xopen on CPython 3.14.2, natively (genomics-wasm's comparison: 34
of 34 cases with human and yeast reads – reads, qualities and JSON statistics; and in the workbench with the example
data): the same trimmed FASTQ files, byte for byte, and the same report.
